verses.gurmukhi: ਸਲਿਲ ਸੁਭਾਵ ਜੈਸੇ ਨਿਵਨ ਗਵਨ ਗੁਨ ਸੀਚੀਅਤ ਉਪਬਨ ਬਿਰਵਾ ਲਗਾਇ ਕੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: salil subhaav jaise nivan gavan gun seecheeat upaban biravaa lagai kai ||

en.bdb: Just as the nature of water is to flow downward, and that enables it to irrigate the plants and saplings planted in the garden,

verses.gurmukhi: ਜਲਿ ਮਿਲਿ ਬਿਰਖਹਿ ਕਰਤ ਉਰਧ ਤਪ ਸਾਖਾ ਨਏ ਸਫਲ ਹੁਇ ਝੁਕ ਰਹੈ ਆਇ ਕੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: jal mil birakheh karat uradh tap saakhaa ne safal hui jhuk rahai aai kai ||

en.bdb: On meeting with water, even the tree goes through the rigours of penance by standing erect and with new branches sprouting and fruit appearing, it bows downward, (its union with water makes it humble).

verses.gurmukhi: ਪਾਹਨ ਹਨਤ ਫਲਦਾਈ ਕਾਟੇ ਹੋਇ ਨਉਕਾ ਲੋਸਟ ਕੈ ਛੇਦੈ ਭੇਦੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਬੰਧਾਇ ਕੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: paahan hanat faladhaiee kaaTe hoi naukaa losaT kai chhedhai bhedhe ba(n)dhan ba(n)dhai kai ||

en.bdb: Having acquired humility from associating with water, it yields fruit even to those who throw stones at it. A boat is made of wood to take people across. The wood is cut, nailed and clipped together. Thus with so many bonds it is able to stay afloat.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪ੍ਰਬਲ ਪ੍ਰਵਾਹ ਸੁਤ ਸਤੁ੍ਰ ਗਹਿ ਪਾਰਿ ਪਰੈ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਸਿਖ ਦੋਖੀ ਤਾਰੈ ਸਮਝਾਇ ਕੈ ॥੪੨੬॥
verses.translit_en: prabal pravaeh sut satur geh paar parai satigur sikh dhokhee taarai samajhai kai ||426||

en.bdb: The rapid flow of water brings the wood and its enemy (iron) alike. Similarly, the humble and philanthropic True Guru does not deliberate on the vices of the slanderers and teaches them the righteousness to takes them across the worldly ocean. (426)
